authors.name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
authors.biography: Dietrich Bonhoeffer (1906–1945) was a German Lutheran pastor, theologian, and anti-Nazi dissident. His writings on Christian ethics and discipleship have been widely read in modern theology. He was executed by the Nazis in April 1945.

authors.name: C.S. Lewis
authors.biography: Clive Staples Lewis (1898–1963) was a British writer, literary scholar, and lay theologian. His works of apologetics, including Mere Christianity, and his Narnia Chronicles have been widely read by Christians and non-Christians alike.

authors.name: Augustine of Hippo
authors.biography: Augustine of Hippo (354–430) was a Roman African bishop, theologian, and philosopher whose writings have been formative for Western Christianity. His Confessions and City of God are widely studied in Christian literature.

authors.name: John Bunyan
authors.biography: John Bunyan (1628–1688) was an English writer and Puritan preacher known for The Pilgrim's Progress, a widely studied work of English literature. He was imprisoned for his nonconformist preaching.

authors.name: J.I. Packer
authors.biography: James Innell Packer (1926–2020) was a British-born Canadian Reformed theologian whose book Knowing God has been widely read in evangelical circles.

authors.name: Richard Foster
authors.biography: Richard Foster is an American theologian and author known for his work on spiritual disciplines. He is the founder of Renovaré, a ministry focused on spiritual formation.

authors.name: John Piper
authors.biography: John Piper is an American Reformed Baptist theologian and pastor, founder of Desiring God ministries. His concept of Christian hedonism has been widely discussed in evangelical theology.

authors.name: John Calvin
authors.biography: John Calvin (1509–1564) was a French theologian, pastor, and reformer in Geneva during the Protestant Reformation. His Institutes of the Christian Religion is a widely studied work of systematic theology.

authors.name: Thomas à Kempis
authors.biography: Thomas à Kempis (c. 1380–1471) was a German-Dutch canon regular and the author of The Imitation of Christ, a widely read devotional book in Christian history.

authors.name: G.K. Chesterton
authors.biography: Gilbert Keith Chesterton (1874–1936) was an English writer, poet, philosopher, and lay theologian. His Orthodoxy and The Everlasting Man are widely discussed works of Christian apologetics.

authors.name: Timothy Keller
authors.biography: Timothy Keller (1950–2023) was an American pastor, theologian, and author. He founded Redeemer Presbyterian Church in New York City and was known for his apologetic approach to urban ministry.
